chat.How to manage tea mosquito bug?:
🐛 **Tea Mosquito Bug (Helopeltis theivora) Management:**

The tea mosquito bug is one of the most destructive pests in Assam tea gardens. It causes characteristic **black lesions and curling of young leaves**, leading to significant crop loss.

**Identification:** Look for brownish-green bugs (6-8mm) on tender shoots. Damage appears as dark brown/black spots on young leaves with curled edges.

**Chemical Control:**
- Apply **Thiamethoxam 25 WG @ 0.2g/litre** as a foliar spray
- Alternatively, use **Imidacloprid 17.8 SL @ 0.3ml/litre**
- ⚠️ **Do NOT spray within 7 days of plucking** (pre-harvest interval)
- Spray early morning or late evening when bugs are most active

**Integrated Management:**
- Maintain **shade trees** (Albizia species) at 40-50% canopy — reduces pest intensity
- Practice **regular plucking** to remove infested shoots
- Encourage natural predators like spiders and ladybird beetles
- Remove alternate host plants (weeds like Mikania) from garden borders

**Prevention:** Monitor fields weekly during March-October (peak season). Economic threshold is **10% shoot infestation** — spray only when this level is reached.
chat.Best fertilizer schedule for Assam tea?:
🌱 **Recommended Fertilizer Schedule for Assam Tea:**

The Tea Research Association recommends a **split application** of NPK fertilizers across 3-4 rounds during the growing season.

**Annual Dose per hectare (mature tea):**
- **Nitrogen (N):** 120-150 kg/ha
- **Phosphorus (P₂O₅):** 50-60 kg/ha
- **Potassium (K₂O):** 60-80 kg/ha

**Application Schedule:**
| Round | Timing | Fertilizer | Rate |
|-------|--------|-----------|------|
| 1st | February-March | Urea + SSP + MOP | 40% of annual dose |
| 2nd | May-June | Urea + MOP | 30% of annual dose |
| 3rd | August-September | Urea + MOP | 30% of annual dose |

**Key Guidelines:**
- Apply fertilizer in a **ring** around the bush drip line, not at the base
- Apply **after rain or irrigation** for better absorption
- For acidic soils (pH < 4.5), apply **Dolomitic limestone @ 2-4 tonnes/ha** every 3 years
- Include **Zinc Sulphate @ 10 kg/ha** annually for micronutrient support
- For organic gardens, use **Neem cake + Vermicompost** as base, supplemented with bio-fertilizers

**Soil Testing:** Get soil tested every year at a TRA-approved lab to fine-tune dosage.
chat.What is the ideal soil pH?:
🧪 **Ideal Soil pH for Assam Tea Cultivation:**

Tea (Camellia sinensis var. assamica) thrives in **acidic soils with pH between 4.5 and 5.5**. This is the optimal range recommended by the Tea Research Association.

**Why pH matters:**
- At pH 4.5-5.5, essential nutrients like **Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium** are most available to tea roots
- **Aluminum toxicity** occurs below pH 4.0, causing root damage
- Above pH 6.0, **iron and manganese deficiency** appears (yellowing of young leaves)

**Corrective Measures:**

| Condition | pH Range | Action |
|-----------|----------|--------|
| Too acidic | Below 4.5 | Apply **Dolomitic limestone @ 2-4 tonnes/ha** |
| Optimal | 4.5 - 5.5 | No correction needed |
| Too alkaline | Above 5.5 | Apply **Aluminium sulphate** or **Sulphur @ 500-1000 kg/ha** |

**Testing Protocol:**
- Collect soil samples from **15-30 cm depth** (root zone)
- Sample during **November-January** (dormant season)
- Test at 3-4 representative spots per section
- Retest every **12 months** to track changes

**Tip:** Organic mulching with tea prunings naturally helps maintain acidic pH over time.
chat.How to improve CTC tea quality?:
☕ **Improving CTC (Crush-Tear-Curl) Tea Quality:**

**1. Plucking Standards (Most Critical):**
- Practice **fine plucking**: 2 leaves + 1 bud only
- Avoid coarse leaves — they increase fibre and reduce briskness
- Pluck at **7-day intervals** during peak season
- Never pluck wet leaves — causes dark liquor and off-flavours

**2. Withering:**
- Target **68-72% wither** for optimal moisture removal
- Wither for **14-18 hours** at 25-30°C
- Physical wither should be 30-40% weight loss
- Chemical wither is complete when leaves feel soft and fold without cracking

**3. CTC Processing:**
- Maintain CTC rollers with **sharp teeth** — dull teeth cause excessive cell damage
- Ensure proper **rotorvane pressure** for uniform maceration
- Fermentation temperature: **24-28°C** for 60-90 minutes
- Monitor fermentation by **colour change** — from green to coppery brown

**4. Drying:**
- Dryer inlet temperature: **120-130°C**
- Outlet temperature: **90-95°C**
- Final moisture content: **2.5-3.5%** (critical for shelf life)

**5. Sorting & Grading:**
- Use proper mesh sizes for grades: BP, BOP, PF, PD, Dust
- Remove **stalk and fibre** using electrostatic separators
- Store in moisture-proof packaging within 24 hours of drying

**Quick Win:** Focus on plucking standards — this alone improves quality by 40-50%.
